A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARISE research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support comparison despite rearrangement and redesigned displays.

before.justification: V1 reports original multi-hop QA experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, model-scaling results and computational-cost analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The decomposition/retrieval procedure, MCTS phases, Risk-Value function and final-path selection remain unchanged. Removing pseudocode and expanding an example change documentation, not the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA and MusiQue. The new dialogue illustrations and expanded Peter Till example do not establish additional evaluated tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same vanilla, prompt-based, search-based, DeepSeek-R1 distilled and MCTS-verifier comparators. The newly cited reward-model papers are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Both retain 200 questions per dataset, the same model configurations and metrics, 200 MCTS iterations, temperature 0.7, UCT weight 1.4 and the documented retrieval/search settings. V2's computational-cost section relocates existing experiments.

E4.justification: V2's final appendix page expands the Peter Till question already illustrated in Figure 2 into a seven-state worked case showing decomposition, accumulated answers and final output. Existing risk-function, iteration, search-space and retrieval analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2 adds no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, ablation, retrieval and timing results are unchanged. The expanded worked case adds the explicit final output 'March 2005', absent from v1's partial illustration; this is a limited qualitative-output addition, not a measured performance improvement.

T1.justification: The assumptions, Bayesian relevance derivation, risk definition and MCTS equations retain the same mathematical content. Section 2.3 restores the missing p in log p(r|q), correcting notation without changing the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same risk-adaptive reasoning contribution and claims about superiority to KAR baselines, comparisons with reasoning models and model scaling.

C2.justification: The revised Limitations replaces discussion of future policy-model training with an argument about static reward models struggling with unseen external knowledge and the need for generalizable rewards. QA-only coverage and prompt concerns remain; adaptive-search limitations were already discussed in v1's appendix.

D1.justification: V2 removes Algorithm 1 and v1 Appendix A.1's disclosure of two NVIDIA H100 GPUs with 80GB memory. It adds a worked reasoning trace while retaining the substantive prompts, hyperparameters, evaluation details and project link.

R1.justification: V2 adds Lightman et al. (2024), Luo et al. (2024) and Wang et al. (2024) to support its discussion of process supervision and reward-model generalization. The main related-work organization and broader positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 makes grammatical and terminology corrections, revises Limitations, updates author information and adds acknowledgements. Computational overhead moves from Appendix A.1 to Section 3.5, but most prose and the overall scientific narrative are retained.

P2.justification: Presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 replaces abstract schematics with dialogue examples; v1 Table 3 becomes v2 Figure 5; the cost-comparison table moves into the main text; Algorithm 1 disappears; and the prompt boxes are reformatted alongside an added full-page worked trace.

improvement.justification: V2 improves accessibility through concrete illustrations, a worked example, copyediting and more prominent cost analysis. However, it removes pseudocode and hardware information and replaces an exact cost table with a plot. With the main scientific evidence unchanged, these clarity gains and losses in technical transparency do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
